predecessors.note: The Hafsid dossier has Barbarossa take Tunis on 16 August 1534 and Charles V enter it on 21 July 1535; the Tunis page has Muley Hasan restored as a vassal.

capitals.name: La Goleta (La Goulette)
capitals.note: The Spanish held the fortress rebuilt by Antonio Ferramolino under Bernardino de Mendoza and, to 1569 and in 1573-1574, Tunis itself as a vassal; the page gives no coordinates, and La Goulette is placed 12 km east of Tunis (10.18 E, 36.80 N in the gazetteer) by the researcher.

The grid cannot separate La Goulette (12 km from Tunis) from Tunis, so one 25 km circle stands for both, and the Hafsid vassal ruler is not subtracted.

ledger.note: 1535: Bizerte comes under Spain. The enclaves table gives 'Bizerte 1535-1573'; the Tunis page mentions Bizerte only as a landmark near the landing at Porto Farina and does not say Spain held it.

July 1535: Charles V takes La Goulette. The assault was set for 14 July after bad weather ('the fortress was taken after the bombardment'; the page gives no capture date outright); 'Charles entered Tunis on July 21'; he 'had Antonio Ferramolino rebuild' La Goulette and left a garrison under Bernardino de Mendoza.

July 1535: Muley Hasan is restored as Spain's vassal. The page has him restored and signing 'a treatise restoring Tunis's vassalage to Spain' (no date for the treaty); Tunis 'remained under Spanish control until its Ottoman recapture in 1569'.
1537: Sousse comes under Spain. The enclaves table gives 'Sousse 1537-1574'; the table names no taker or holder.
1550: Monastir and Mahdia come under Spain. The table gives 'Monastir 1550-1554' and 'Mahdia 1550-1553'; no page opened says from whom.
1553: Mahdia is lost. The enclaves table gives 'Mahdia 1550-1553'; no page opened names the taker.
1554: Monastir is lost. The enclaves table gives 'Monastir 1550-1554'.
1569: the Ottomans recapture Tunis. 'The Ottomans recaptured Tunis in 1569'; the table keeps La Goulette Spanish to 1574, so the fortress stayed.
1573: Bizerte is lost. The enclaves table gives 'Bizerte 1535-1573'.
October 1573: John of Austria re-conquers Tunis. 'October 1573 (no day given): John of Austria re-conquered Tunis'; the enclaves table gives 'Tunis 1573-1574'. The page names no ruler installed.

24 August - 13 September 1574: the Ottomans take La Goleta and Tunis. The campaign ran 12 July - 13 September 1574; 'La Goleta (La Goulette) fell' on 24 August and 'the last Christian troops in the small fort opposite Tunis surrendered' on 13 September; the battle 'marked the final establishment of Ottoman rule in Tunis'.
1574: the Spanish presence in Tunisia ends. The battle ended 'the Hafsid dynasty and the Spanish presence there' (the page gives no separate year); the table gives Sousse to 1574.

wars.name: Charles V's conquest of Tunis
wars.outcome: The armada sailed from Sardinia on 14 June 1535, landed at Porto Farina and finished disembarking on 17 June; La Goulette fell after the bombardment of mid-July; Charles entered Tunis on 21 July; Barbarossa fled towards Bona and Algiers.

wars.name: Don John's Tunis and the Ottoman reconquest
wars.outcome: John of Austria reconquered Tunis in October 1573; the Ottoman campaign of 12 July - 13 September 1574 took La Goleta (24 August) against a presidio 'defended by 7,000 men' and the small fort opposite Tunis (13 September).

certainty.note: A string of coastal presidios: the pages give years and no extent; each is a 25 km circle, the grid's minimum.

notes: Cliopatria has no Spanish Tunis row. The Hafsid dossier holds the Hafsid side: the vassalage and the occupation of Tunis 1535-1569 and 1573-1574 under the counterpart spanish-empire and the Ottoman events under ottoman-empire; this dossier uses ottoman-empire for the Spanish gains and losses. Page conflicts: the Conquest of Tunis (1574) page gives the fall of La Goleta as 24 August; the Conquest of Tunis (1535) page names no capture date for La Goulette (14 July is the date set for the assault) and does not say Spain held Bizerte. The enclaves table gives Bizerte, Sousse, Monastir and Mahdia years with no text; those four are confidence 2 and the grid cannot show a presidio smaller than 25 km. Not entered: Annaba (1535-1540), Honaine (1531-1535) and Djerba (1521-1524, 1559-1560), which are Algerian or island holdings of the same table. The 1569-1573 interval is Ottoman at Tunis and the table keeps La Goulette Spanish throughout; the 1574 page says the presidio was 'defended by 7,000 men'. The Tunis page does not use the word 'protectorate' for the Hafsid relationship (the enclaves table does).
